bull_case_summary: Tenaga has RM1.8018bn cash after specified finance and both lease components versus RM1.6322bn dividends. Round two emphasises actual cost-inclusive coverage and modest operating-profit growth as support for conditional utility income at 16.83x earnings.
bear_case_summary: The bear accepts funded period income but stresses only RM169.6m residual alongside RM60.936bn borrowings and RM31.198bn leases. Lower margin and owners earnings plus regulated collection timing keep downside protection thinner than coverage alone suggests.
key_points_of_agreement: Residual cash is narrow rather than abundant.
Large obligations and restricted/longer-tenor deposits remain relevant.
key_points_of_disagreement: How far demonstrated income coverage compensates heavy obligations and regulated cash-timing sensitivity.
unresolved_uncertainties: Future tariff/fuel reconciliation and regulated investment returns.
Persistence of cost-inclusive coverage through cash-timing changes and grid investment.
